predecessors.name: mbata
predecessors.text: the kingdom 'was founded around 1390 through the political marriage' of the Kongo-speaking peoples of Mbata and Mpemba Kasi; Lukeni's new base was the mountain Mongo dia Kongo

predecessors.name: Mpemba Kasi
predecessors.text: Lukeni 'expanded south' into Mpemba lands and allied with the Mwene Kabunga

successors.name: Portuguese Angola
successors.text: the capital Mbanza Kongo (São Salvador) and its hinterland

capitals.name: Mbanza Kongo (São Salvador from the late 16th century)

ledger.x: c. 1390: the Kingdom of Kongo is founded at Mbanza Kongo. 'The kingdom of Kongo was founded around 1390 through the political marriage between the two' peoples; infobox 'Conquest of Kabunga: 1390'. The page gives no boundary.
1509 onward: Afonso I extends the kingdom.
1526: Afonso reconquers the rebel province of Mpanzalumbu.
1623 January: Kongo defeats the Portuguese at Mbanda Kasi and the invasion of Mbamba ends.
1641: Daniel da Silva takes Soyo and defies Garcia II.
ledger.cp: Soyo (county of Kongo, then independent Counts and Grand Princes of Soyo)

ledger.x: 1656: Garcia II's last attempt on Soyo fails and the province stays out of his control.
ledger.cp: Soyo (county of Kongo, then independent Counts and Grand Princes of Soyo)

ledger.x: 1656: Soyo is lost to the crown.
ledger.cp: Soyo (county of Kongo, then independent Counts and Grand Princes of Soyo)

ledger.x: 1678: São Salvador is sacked and abandoned.
1709 February 15: Pedro IV marches on São Salvador and the kingdom is reunified after the civil war of 1665-1709.
1709 February 15: the king re-enters São Salvador, the capital again from 1709.
1859: Pedro V swears vassalage to Portugal and the kingdom becomes a titular Portuguese vassal.
1884-1885: the Berlin Conference divides the old kingdom.
1885: the Congo-side lands pass to the Independent State of the Congo (Berlin Conference 1884-1885); see the Portuguese entry for the page's wording.

wars.name: Jaga invasion of Kongo
wars.outcome: Jaga raiders overran the kingdom; Álvaro I's rule begins amid the crisis and he later allows a Portuguese colony in Luanda.

wars.name: First Kongo-Portuguese War
wars.outcome: Portugal invaded Mbamba (Mbumbi); Kongo defeated the Portuguese at Mbanda Kasi in January 1623.

wars.name: Kongo campaigns against Soyo
wars.outcome: Garcia II's attempts on Soyo in 1641, 1643, 1645 and 1656 all failed; Soyo was independent by the end of his reign.

wars.name: Portuguese-Dutch war in Angola (Kongo as Dutch ally)
wars.outcome: The Dutch took Luanda in 1641 and allied with Kongo; Kongo troops helped Queen Nzinga defeat the Portuguese at Kombi in 1647; the Dutch withdrew in 1648 and Portugal held Luanda by 1649.

wars.name: Battle of Mbwila
wars.outcome: Portuguese forces defeated Kongo on 29 October 1665 and King António I was killed; Portugal obtained an act of vassalage from D.

wars.name: Kongo Civil War
wars.outcome: 'The Kongo Civil War (1665-1709)' between the Kinlaza and Kimpanzu houses, with the Água Rosada of Kibangu and the da Silva of Soyo taking part; São Salvador was burnt in 1678 and Pedro IV re-entered it on 15 February 1709; Mbata and Nsundi broke away.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is given by the pages; the kingdom's provinces and frontiers are approximate.
